docs.title: Data
docs.text:
python -m ocen_dm.cli fetch-data    # registered downloads, checksums verified
python -m ocen_dm.cli preprocess    # standardised catalogues and published profiles
python -m ocen_dm.cli plot-data
  • Two journal supplements need manual retrieval.
  • Our own HST and Gaia PM profiles and the count products have separate builders (kinematics/hst_profile.py, kinematics/outer_gaia.py, bin/build_count_profiles.py). Loaders build missing products automatically, so a fresh checkout can write data on first use.
  • External catalogues live in a shared store ($OCEN_CATALOGUES) and are referenced, not copied; some model inputs come from a clone of oCen_bar. See Data products.

docs.title: Fitting
docs.text:
• Fits are launched only when requested, with a fresh output label; a run directory is never reused. Every batch freezes its source, configuration and inputs (with sha256), so it can be replayed exactly.
  • The base model is fitted with bin/run_compact_df_recovery.py; the exact command is on the base model page.
  • The older Jeans fits use python -m ocen_dm.cli fit with explicit switches (see the modelling plan); a bare fit selects an outdated default.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
python -m pytest tests -q

The full suite includes local-data and optional-engine tests and takes tens of minutes; some tests skip without those inputs.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Units: internal dynamics in pc, M☉ and km/s; Galactic-orbit modules carry their own explicit conversions (AGAMA time unit = 977.8 Myr).
  • Plots are PNG files in plots/; plotted tables and JSON provenance go to results/plot_data/. Compiled PDFs sit next to their LaTeX in docs/.
  • data/ and results/ are not committed.
  • Results are recorded in a project journal that is kept locally (not in git); the reports in docs/ carry the results that are shared.
  • External reviews go to docs/reviews/.

docs.title: Comparison with published mass models
docs.text:
How our two no-DM models (the DF base model and the Jeans comparison model) compare with published models of Omega Centauri's mass distribution. Published numbers are taken from the papers' abstracts (checked in ADS, 2026-10-14) unless marked otherwise; all papers are in the SciX library.

Summary

  • Total mass and M/L agree within the spread of published values. Our total M/L_V of 2.8 is close to Watkins+2013 (2.71); our total mass, 3.26×10⁶ M☉, is 13–22% below the recent estimates of 3.7–4.2×10⁶ M☉ (D'Souza & Rix 2013 scaled to our distance; the Baumgardt database).
  • The central dark mass is where the literature splits, and our two models fall on the two sides. The Jeans model's 4.3×10⁴ M☉ black hole reproduces the classic IMBH claims (Noyola+2008/2010, Baumgardt 2017, Jalali+2012). The DF model's compact remnant component (2.7×10⁵ M☉, 2.2 pc scale, 8% of the mass, no black hole) matches the "extended central mass" picture: 2–3×10⁵ M☉ favoured by kinematics plus pulsar timing (Bañares-Hernández+2025: 2.65×10⁵ M☉ in a Plummer of 1.88 pc, the same form, mass and nearly the same scale as ours) and ~5% of the mass in stellar-mass black holes (Zocchi+2019, Baumgardt+2019, Dickson+2024).
  • Anisotropy: the DF profile (isotropic core, mildly radial at intermediate radii, tangential outside) agrees with oMEGACat VI and van de Ven+2006; the Jeans model's tangential core does not.
  • Not yet tested: whether the DF model accommodates the ≥ 8,200 M☉ black hole implied by the fast-moving stars (Häberle+2024).

docs.title: Total mass, mass-to-light ratio and distance
docs.text:
Proper-motion-based masses scale as \(M\propto D^3\) and M/L as \(\propto D\); published values are given at their own distance, and scaled to ours (5.356 kpc) only where the paper states the scaling.

Study Method D [kpc] Total mass [10⁶ M☉] M/L_V This work, DF base model spherical action DF, HST+MUSE+Gaia kinematics, star counts 5.356 (prior 5.43 ± 0.05) 3.26 2.8 (stellar 2.6) This work, Jeans model spherical Jeans, black hole, same kinematics 5.34–5.36 3.18–3.24 2.7–2.8 (stellar 2.0–2.3) van de Ven+2006 axisymmetric Schwarzschild, ground-based PMs + LOS 4.8 ± 0.3 (fitted) 2.5 ± 0.3 2.5 ± 0.1 Watkins+2013 discrete axisymmetric Jeans 4.59 ± 0.08 (fitted) — 2.71 ± 0.05 D'Souza & Rix 2013 discrete PM likelihood scaled to 5.356 4.20 (spherical isotropic), 3.74 (flattened) — Baumgardt GC database N-body grid (catalogue value; version unrecorded, UNVERIFIED against the live database) 5.43 3.94 — Merritt+1997 non-parametric, 469 LOS velocities — — mass "slightly more extended than" the light

D'Souza & Rix give \(4.55\times10^6\,(D/5.5\,{\rm kpc})^3\) M☉ (spherical) and \(4.05\times10^6\,(D/5.5\,{\rm kpc})^3\) M☉ (flattened); at 5.356 kpc the factor is 0.923.

  • M/L is close to published values: our total M/L_V of 2.8 is slightly above Watkins (2.71) and van de Ven (2.5). Scaled to our distance with M/L ∝ D their values would be 3.2 and 2.8; their distances were fitted jointly, so this scaling is only indicative.
  • Our total mass is 13–22% below the recent estimates at our distance (3.26 against 3.74–4.20×10⁶ M☉ from D'Souza & Rix and 3.94×10⁶ M☉ from the Baumgardt database). van de Ven+2006 found 2.5×10⁶ M☉ at 4.8 kpc. Possible reasons, not yet tested: our model is spherical (D'Souza & Rix find flattening lowers the mass by 10%, in the same direction, so it does not explain it); our kinematics reach ~60 pc and the mass beyond is extrapolated; the Gaia data may have systematics in the outer bins; and the Baumgardt value comes from mass-segregated N-body models.
  • Distance: ours (5.356 kpc) is pulled by the prior; the oMEGACat VI kinematic distance is 5.494 ± 0.061 kpc (Häberle+2025), 2.2σ larger. At 5.494 kpc our proper-motion masses would be ~8% higher.

docs.title: The central dark mass
docs.text:
Study Method Central dark mass This work, Jeans model spherical Jeans, β₀ ≤ −½ imposed IMBH 4.3 (3.6–4.9) ×10⁴ M☉ (95%) This work, DF base model self-consistent DF, isotropic core no IMBH; remnants 2.7×10⁵ M☉ in a 2.2 pc Plummer (8% of the mass) Noyola+2008 isotropic spherical, Gemini + HST IMBH 4.0 (+0.75/−1.0) ×10⁴ M☉ Noyola+2010 VLT kinematics IMBH (4.7 ± 1.0) ×10⁴ M☉ Jalali+2012 N-body, isotropic multimass King ICs IMBH 5×10⁴ M☉ (2% of the stellar mass) Baumgardt 2017 N-body grid IMBH ~4×10⁴ M☉ van der Marel & Anderson 2010 anisotropic spherical Jeans, HST PMs core models fit with M_BH = 0; M_BH ≲ 1.2×10⁴ (1σ), ≲ 1.8×10⁴ M☉ (3σ) Zocchi+2017 radially anisotropic limepy central kinematics fitted without an IMBH Zocchi+2019 multimass limepy ~5% of the mass in stellar-mass black holes Baumgardt+2019 N-body grid + fast-star test no IMBH; 4.6% of the mass in a central cluster of stellar-mass black holes Evans+2022 axisymmetric Jeans, dark + luminous components non-luminous component ≲ 10⁶ M☉ within r_h preferred over constant M/L; a compact remnant core can supply up to ~5×10⁵ M☉ Dickson+2024 multimass models black-hole mass fraction above 5% Häberle+2024 seven fast-moving stars in the central 3″ (0.08 pc) IMBH ≥ 8,200 M☉ (firm lower limit) Bañares-Hernández+2025 Jeans (GravSphere) + millisecond-pulsar accelerations extended central mass ~2–3×10⁵ M☉ favoured over an IMBH; IMBH < 6×10³ M☉ (3σ)
  • Our two models reproduce the two sides of the debate with the same data. The black-hole mass of our Jeans model is the classic value (4–5×10⁴ M☉). That value comes from models with isotropic or imposed central anisotropy; in ours the black hole is tied to β₀ at its −½ bound and gains Δχ² ≈ 6 from a few bins inside 0.3 pc.
  • The DF model's dark mass is the "extended central mass". Its remnant component, 2.7×10⁵ M☉ with a 2.2 pc scale (half-mass radius 2.8 pc), matches the 2–3×10⁵ M☉ that Bañares-Hernández+2025 favour from kinematics and pulsar timing, the ~5% stellar-mass black-hole fraction of Zocchi+2019, Baumgardt+2019 and Dickson+2024, and the ≲ 5×10⁵ M☉ remnant core that Evans+2022 allow. Our component is a generic Plummer, so it can also contain white dwarfs and neutron stars.
  • A small IMBH is not excluded by either picture. The fast-star lower limit (≥ 8,200 M☉, Häberle+2024) is 0.25% of the cluster mass. It lies below the 3σ upper limit of van der Marel & Anderson (1.8×10⁴ M☉) but above the 3σ upper limit of Bañares-Hernández+2025 (6×10³ M☉), a tension between those two published results. Our DF model has no point mass; adding one of ~10⁴ M☉ at fixed everything else is the natural next test.

docs.title: Remnant mass and spatial scale
docs.text:
Numbers from the full texts (arXiv versions, read 2026-10-14), with their location in each paper. Values marked computed are ours, derived from the paper's numbers as shown.

Study Component (definition) Mass [M☉] Fraction Form and scale Total mass, distance Where This work, DF base model remnant Plummer: all mass not following the counted light 2.73×10⁵ 8.4% Plummer, a = 2.18 pc (3D; half-mass 2.85 pc) 3.26×10⁶, 5.356 kpc base model This work, Jeans model remnant Plummer + black hole 5.4×10⁵ + 4.3×10⁴ 16.5% + 1.3% Plummer, a = 5.3 pc (3D) 3.24×10⁶, 5.36 kpc Jeans model Bañares-Hernández+2025 "extended central mass" on top of a light-traced M★ (which includes remnants that follow the light); interpreted as stellar-mass black holes 2.65 ± 0.19×10⁵; 2.20×10⁵ without the pulsar accelerations; 2.1–3.1×10⁵ across centres and profile shapes 9.0% (computed: 2.65/(26.8+2.65)) Plummer, r_cen = 1.88 ± 0.10 pc (3D; 1.59 pc without pulsars); Gaussian alternative σ = 1.37 pc M★ = 2.68 ± 0.05×10⁶; 5.2 kpc fixed Fig. 2, Table 2, Secs. 6, 8–9, App. B–D Baumgardt+2019 stellar-mass black holes only 1.65×10⁵ 4.6 ± 0.5% mass-segregated N-body; radius not given ("centrally concentrated") 5.24 kpc adopted Secs. 4–5 Zocchi+2019 black holes as the dark component of two-component limepy models (white dwarfs and neutron stars in the visible component) 1.35×10⁵ (computed: F₂ × M) 4.5 (+4.0/−2.5)% anisotropic; 5.2% isotropic not fully segregated, extending to about the half-mass radius (r_h = 8.57 pc); ~1.4×10³ M☉ within 0.2 pc 3.01×10⁶, 5.14 kpc (fitted) Table 2, Secs. 3–4 Dickson+2024 (i) black holes; (ii) all dark remnants (white dwarfs, neutron stars, black holes) (i) 1.82×10⁵ (12,400 black holes, mean 14.8 M☉) (i) 5.9 ± 0.2% (statistical only); (ii) 50.3% multimass limepy; radius not given ("concentrated within the central regions") in their Paper I Table 1, Sec. 5.3 Evans+2022 generic non-luminous component (remnants or dark matter) 10⁴–10⁶ within the ~6 pc half-light radius (posterior contours only) — NFW with r_max ≲ 1 pc (r_s = r_max/2.16), or Gaussian 5.24 kpc fixed Secs. 6–7, Figs. 5, 7

Like-for-like with the closest model (Bañares-Hernández+2025, same Plummer form):

DF base model Bañares-Hernández+2025 Mass 2.73×10⁵ M☉ 2.65 ± 0.19×10⁵ M☉ Plummer scale 2.18 pc 1.88 ± 0.10 pc at 5.2 kpc; 1.94 pc scaled to 5.356 kpc (computed) Mass fraction 8.4% 9.0% M(<1 pc), M(<3 pc) (computed) 2.0×10⁴, 1.45×10⁵ M☉ 2.7×10⁴, 1.61×10⁵ M☉ Data HST, MUSE, Gaia kinematics; star counts stellar kinematics, surface density, millisecond-pulsar positions and accelerations Method self-consistent action DF Jeans (GravSphere)
  • The DF remnant component reproduces the Bañares-Hernández central mass: the same mass within 3%, a scale 12% larger once both are at the same distance, and the same mass fraction. They reach it with a different method and with pulsar timing; from stellar kinematics alone they find a smaller and more compact component (2.20×10⁵ M☉, 1.59 pc).
  • The black-hole-only estimates are lower, 1.35–1.82×10⁵ M☉ (4.5–5.9%). That is expected: our component also holds whatever neutron stars and segregated white dwarfs do not follow the light, whereas those models put white dwarfs and neutron stars in the visible or light-traced mass (in Dickson+2024 all dark remnants make up 50% of the mass).
  • Scales: besides Bañares-Hernández, only Evans+2022 constrain one (r_max ≲ 1 pc for an NFW), and Zocchi+2019 give a qualitative extent (to about the half-mass radius, 8.6 pc). The concentration differs between models: within 0.2 pc Zocchi's black-hole component holds ~1.4×10³ M☉, against ~300 M☉ for the Bañares-Hernández Plummer and ~200 M☉ for ours (computed for the Plummer models).
  • The Jeans model's remnant component (5.4×10⁵ M☉ at 5.3 pc) is twice as massive and 2.5 times more extended than any of these; its central mass is carried by the black hole instead.
  • Our remnant mass is the least constrained of our numbers. It trades against the stellar mass (±23% on mocks), and pinning the mass per counted star between 8 and 12 M☉ moves it from 1.6 to 4.4×10⁵ M☉.

Caveat: the Bañares-Hernández values are from arXiv:2408.00939v6, which may differ in detail from the journal version; in it, the Sec. 8.1 statement on the centre dependence does not match the Fig. C.1 numbers.

docs.title: Anisotropy
docs.text:
Study Anisotropy This work, DF base model isotropic core; radial, peak β ≈ +0.15 near 8 pc; tangential beyond ~22 pc (−0.53 at 100 pc) This work, Jeans model tangential core (β₀ ≈ −0.52, imposed ≤ −½); radial +0.15 at 3–15 pc; tangential outside Häberle+2025 (oMEGACat VI) isotropic in the core, increasing radial anisotropy outwards (HST field) Watkins+2013 mildly radial, β = 0.10 ± 0.02 (single value) van de Ven+2006 close to isotropic inside ~10′, increasingly tangential outside Zocchi+2017 radially anisotropic models fit the central kinematics
  • The DF profile matches the published picture: isotropic core, radially biased within the HST field, tangential in the outskirts. Our zero crossing (~22 pc, 14′ at our distance) is near van de Ven's ~10′ transition.
  • The Jeans model's tangential core disagrees with the isotropic core measured directly by oMEGACat VI. It is a consequence of the black hole (a cored tracer around a point mass needs β₀ ≤ −½), which is a further argument against taking its black-hole mass at face value.

docs.title: Dark matter
docs.text: Evans+2022 find a non-luminous component of ≲ 10⁶ M☉ within the half-light radius strongly preferred over a constant-M/L stellar model and leave open that part of it is dark matter. Our models agree that a centrally concentrated non-luminous mass is needed (2.7×10⁵ M☉ in the DF model, ~6×10⁵ M☉ of remnants plus black hole in the Jeans model), but find that it can be supplied by remnants without dark matter. Our dark-matter variants show that the data constrain the total mass profile, not how it splits between stars, remnants and dark matter (Results).

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• No comparison yet with published axisymmetric or rotating models on our data; ours are spherical.
  • The published total masses use different data and extents; a like-for-like test (our pipeline on their data, or theirs on ours) has not been done.
  • Earlier literature numbers assembled for the Jeans fits: Literature baselines.

docs.title: Base model fits
docs.text: The reference result of the project: the base no-DM model (two-transition action DF for the stars, a Plummer remnant component, no dark matter, no central black hole) fitted jointly to 89 kinematic bins and the HST and Gaia star counts.

docs.text:
Batch results/df/dftwo_counts_area_20261013, refitted after the count-likelihood correction. All four valid starts reach the same minimum (objectives within 0.01); numerical validation passes; no parameter sits at a bound.

docs.title: Comparison with the Jeans model (dashed curves)
docs.text:
Full description, figures and posterior: Jeans comparison model.

The dashed curves are the best rung-2 spherical Jeans fit without dark matter (results/fits/rung2_K1_turnover), the best model of the earlier Jeans ladder. Both models are fitted to the same 89-bin kinematic snapshot, so their kinematic χ² compare directly; the Jeans fit uses a fixed light profile (an MGE of the Trager+1995 profile joined to HST star counts) instead of the Poisson star counts.

Jeans (rung 2, no DM) DF base model Stellar tracer and mass MGE light profile, mass-to-light free self-consistent action DF Free stellar parameters \(M_\star\) only (density shape fixed by the light) \(M_\star\) and six DF parameters (shape fitted to the counts) Anisotropy turnover β(r): β₀ = −0.50 (centre) → +0.20 → −0.98 (outside) isotropic core → +0.15 near 8 pc → −0.53 at 100 pc Central black hole 4.4×10⁴ M☉ (16–84%: 3.9–4.6×10⁴) none \(M_\star\) 2.37×10⁶ M☉ 3.00×10⁶ M☉ Remnants (Plummer) 7.7×10⁵ M☉, a = 5.7 pc 2.7×10⁵ M☉, a = 2.2 pc Total mass 3.18×10⁶ M☉ 3.26×10⁶ M☉ \(M_\star/L_V\), \(M_{\rm tot}/L_V\) 2.0, 2.7 (ML); 2.3, 2.8 (median) 2.6, 2.8 Distance 5.34 kpc 5.36 kpc χ² (per bin) Jeans DF HST PM radial (21) 61.8 (2.94) 42.6 (2.03) HST PM tangential (21) 36.6 (1.74) 39.8 (1.89) MUSE LOS (29) 51.7 (1.78) 38.1 (1.31) Gaia PM radial (9) 16.9 (1.88) 14.4 (1.60) Gaia PM tangential (9) 23.0 (2.56) 21.5 (2.39) Total (89) 190.0 156.4
  • The DF fits better overall (Δχ² = 34) and in every dataset except the HST tangential proper motions.
  • The Jeans model follows the central rise of the HST proper-motion dispersions inside 0.3 pc (~11″), which the DF, with an isotropic core and no black hole, stays below by 1.5–2.4σ in several bins: χ² = 7.3 (Jeans) against 21.5 (DF) for those 10 bins. This is where the black hole matters.
  • It pays for this at intermediate radii: at 2–20 pc (36 bins of HST, MUSE and Gaia) χ² = 122.2 (Jeans) against 77.8 (DF), mostly in the HST radial proper motions (40.2 against 20.2) and the MUSE line-of-sight dispersions (30.9 against 18.7).
  • The black hole is tied to an imposed anisotropy. A cored stellar density around a point mass needs β₀ ≤ −½ for any non-negative DF; the prior enforces it and the fit sits at the bound (β₀ = −0.503). Even so, under the standard separable construction a non-negative DF fails to exist at 0.02–0.18 pc, where the black hole dominates (89.7% of posterior draws fail; no failure outside ~0.2 pc; a non-separable DF is not excluded; DF consistency audit). The DF base model is non-negative by construction.
  • Both put about the same total mass in the cluster (3.2–3.3×10⁶ M☉) but divide it differently: the Jeans fit has 20% less stellar mass and nearly three times more remnant mass, spread over a 2.5× larger scale. This is the same stars-versus-dark-mass degeneracy seen within the DF fits.
  • Why \(M_\star\) differs by 11% at the same total mass. In neither model is the stellar mass fixed by the light or the counts; it is the normalisation the kinematics leave after the remnants (and, for Jeans, the black hole and the imposed central anisotropy) take their share. The remnant mass is close to the total minus \(M_\star\), so with remnants at 8–17% of the total, a 1% change in \(M_\star\) moves \(M_{\rm rem}\) by ~10%.
  • A central black hole was not supported by the DF fits on binned data (September step 3); whether the inner rise needs one, or radially biased central orbits, or mass segregation, is not settled.

docs.title: Mass components
docs.text:
Current fit, by component. (a) Density; (b) enclosed mass with the half-mass radii dotted; (c) circular velocity; (d) remnant share, local (\(\rho_{\rm rem}/\rho_{\rm tot}\)) and cumulative (\(M_{\rm rem}/M_{\rm tot}\)); (e) dynamical-to-stellar mass ratio. Grey: outside the radial range of the kinematic data (0.1–63 pc).

r (pc) Stars (10⁶ M☉) Remnants (10⁶ M☉) Total (10⁶ M☉) Remnant share of M(<r) 1 0.012 0.020 0.032 62% 3 0.201 0.145 0.346 42% 10 1.436 0.255 1.691 15% 30 2.716 0.271 2.987 9% 100 2.987 0.273 3.260 8%
  • Two components with different scales. The stars have a 3D half-mass radius of 10.4 pc (projected 7.7 pc; the Baumgardt database lists r_h = 7.56 pc at 5.43 kpc, i.e. 7.46 pc at the fitted distance); the remnant Plummer has 2.8 pc.
  • The remnants dominate the core. They are 66% of the central density (6.0×10³ against 3.2×10³ M☉ pc⁻³ for the stars at 0.3 pc). The stars take over the local density near 1.5 pc (remnants 59% at 1 pc, 26% at 3 pc) and the enclosed mass near 2 pc.
  • Mass-to-light-following mass. \(M_{\rm tot}(<r)/M_\star(<r)\) falls from 2.9 in the centre to 1.09 overall. This is the quantity a mass-segregated stellar population could also produce.
  • Circular velocity peaks at 27.0 km/s at 9.0 pc; the stars alone peak at ~25 km/s near 10 pc, the remnants at ~14 km/s near 3 pc. The central escape speed is 68 km/s.
  • The total inside 10 pc differs from the superseded fit by −0.7%.

docs.title: Internal kinematics
docs.text:
(a) Intrinsic radial and tangential (one component) dispersions, with the local escape speed/√12 for scale; (b) anisotropy β(r); (c) stellar surface density with the projected and 3D half-mass radii; (d) projected line-of-sight and proper-motion dispersions from the DF, before the published rotation is subtracted in the likelihood.

  • Isotropic core, radial bias at intermediate radii, tangential outskirts. β = 0.00 at 0.3 pc, 0.09 at 3 pc, peaks at +0.15 near 8 pc, crosses zero near 22 pc, and reaches −0.08 at 30 pc and −0.53 at 100 pc.
  • Central dispersion σ_r ≈ σ_t ≈ 21.4 km/s; σ_r = 14.7 and σ_t = 13.5 km/s at 10 pc.
  • Projected dispersions in the core: 19.8 km/s along the line of sight and 19.3 km/s in each proper-motion component. The radial and tangential proper-motion profiles differ by ≲ 0.5 km/s inside 30 pc and separate in the tangentially biased outskirts.

docs.title: Distribution function
docs.text:
(a) Intrinsic moments and β(r); (b) the anisotropy bias \(b(q)\), \(q=J_r+L\), over the action distributions of the stars in the HST/MUSE (R ≤ 9.5 pc) and Gaia (9.4–63 pc) ranges, with the two transitions \(J_a\) and \(J_{\rm outer}\) dotted; (c) \(f(J_r, L)\).

  • The radial bias (b ≈ +0.45 at its peak) sits on the actions of the HST/MUSE stars; the tangential tail (b → −0.33) sits on the Gaia stars. The data constrain the DF over \(q\) ≈ 10–1000 pc km/s; outside that range its shape is extrapolated.
  • \(f\) is smooth and monotonic in both actions, with no features at the transitions.

docs.title: What the base fits establish
docs.text:
• No dark matter is needed to fit the kinematics and counts. A free cored halo goes to \(\rho_{20}=0\) (2026-09-23, old count likelihood).
  • The total mass profile is constrained; its split is not. Mocks drawn from the base model recover the total mass to ±3% at 20 pc and ±5% over 2–40 pc, but stars trade against remnants plus halo through the count amplitude, and the recovered \(\rho_{20}\) scatters by ±0.7 M☉ pc⁻³.
  • The answer depends on the stellar mass per counted star. Fixed at the photometric 8–9 M☉ per F625W < 19 star, the data prefer \(\rho_{20}\) ≈ 2–4; at the dynamical value (now 10.5) they prefer none. The photometric estimate (8.3–9.8 in the zones that dominate the kinematics) is not precise enough (~1 M☉ per star; ~0.3 is needed) to decide.
  • The fit is not statistically acceptable. χ²_kin per bin is 1.76 against the gate of 1.3, and the HST count residuals are structured: data below the model near 1 pc and in the outermost HST bin (~6 pc), above it at 3–4 pc. Either the error bars are underestimated or the model lacks freedom (mass segregation, rotation, a different remnant shape); this is not yet separated.

docs.text: The free-halo fit, the \(\rho_{20}\) profile, the mass-per-star scan and the mocks (all 2026-09-23). See Models and the DF observed-fit write-up (PDF); data analysis (PDF).

docs.title: Dark-matter survival and tidal tails
docs.text:
• Restricted and live N-body runs of a no-DM and a DM model on Omega Cen's orbit (static McMillan17, 1.96 Gyr) give tails whose kinematics agree to 10%. The DM model loses 1.3–1.6× fewer stars. Neither difference is testable with the published tail data (Kuzma+2021, Kuzma+2026, Ibata+2019).
  • Fitted halos are compact (r_s at the 5 pc bound) and traded against stellar mass, so across the kinematically allowed range the Jacobi radius at pericentre changes by ≤ 6.5%. Dark matter that could affect the tails lies beyond ~80–200 pc and is not constrained by the kinematics.

Reports: dynamical experiments, first batch (PDF), batch analysis, progenitor orbits, Section-11 tests, lifetime evolution (paused), DM capture constraints (PDF), N-body code assessment, N-body ICs.

docs.title: Stream 54 (Fimbulthul) and the proper-motion knee
docs.text:
• Beyond φ1 ≈ 17° the stream bends in Gaia DR3 proper motion. No published model reproduces this, nor do sprays in static McMillan17 or DB98 hosts.
  • A rotating Hunter+2024 bar bends the arm part-way and steepens the pmdec gradient. Bar angle 16° beats 28° by ~285 in ln L on held-out seeds (paired seed sd 101); the distal PM residual remains.
  • The LMC (rigid MW + LMC, reflex frame, benchmarked against the Tango N-body runs) shifts distal pmra by 0.2–0.6 mas/yr, but a 0.03–0.05 mas/yr change in Omega Cen's PM absorbs it.
  • Spiral forcing, the conditional likelihood's density dependence, the Chen+2024 escape law and both launch arms do not remove the mismatch.
  • Backtracked in the barred host, the 13 knee RV stars connect to the cluster much worse than model controls (1.9–2.0 against ~1.1). This is a mismatch in the recent (≤ 700 Myr) fixed-potential models tested, not yet an exclusion.

Reports: PM refinement (current), knee investigation, diagnostic plan, fit campaign plan, experiments plan, stream-fitting methods review, stream distances literature.

docs.title: Key facts
docs.text:
• Baseline inputs. The current baseline DF likelihood is results/df/dftwo_counts_20260923. It uses:
  • five kinematic profiles: hst_pm_radial_ours, hst_pm_tangential_ours, muse_los_dispersion, gaia_edr3_ours_radial, gaia_edr3_ours_tangential (89 bins in total);
  • two Poisson count profiles: ocen_counts_hst_f625w19 (20 bins) and ocen_counts_gaia_g17 (12 bins).

The kinematics are frozen in observed/data_snapshot.json (sha256 570399f3…). That snapshot was copied from results/df/pilot_no_dm_20260922, which took it from the Jeans run results/fits/rung2_K1_turnover. The rung-1 and rung-2 Jeans ladder runs carry the identical snapshot sha. - Products reproduce the baseline. I reloaded the five profiles today through ocen_dm.kinematics.likelihood.load_profile. Values and errors match the frozen snapshot exactly (max |Δ|/σ = 0). This holds even though ocen_pm_dispersion_edr3_ours.ecsv was rebuilt on 2026-10-11. - Count products have moved on. The baseline used schema-1 count files (star-weighted quantile nodes). Their sha256 values match proc/kinematics/ocen_counts_*_schema1_20260923.json. The files proc/kinematics/ocen_counts_*.json now hold schema 2 (area-weighted covered-area quadrature, commit 1af8c33). A rerun with the current products would therefore not reproduce the baseline count deviance. - Indirect baseline inputs. Several products feed the baseline without being likelihood terms themselves:

Product How it reaches the baseline Vasiliev & Baumgardt (2021) PM profiles PM rotation curve used for the tangential streaming subtraction and its error oMEGACat LOS rotation MUSE streaming term Gaia DR3 field template from WSDB Used by both of our own PM-dispersion builders Composite tracer profile (Trager 1995 plus oMEGACat selection_hq_f625w star counts) Gaia depth-dispersion correction Vasiliev & Baumgardt member catalogue Parent sample for the Gaia PMs and the Gaia counts oMEGACat star catalogue Parent sample for the HST PMs and the HST counts
  • Main gaps. Detailed in Section 3:
  • The registry (provenance/datasets.yaml) covers only the September kinematics/tails datasets. All stream-project inputs are registered only in configs/data.yaml or the project journal, or not at all: STREAMFINDER 2021/2024, HST LP, the Tango Zenodo archive, Hunter+2024 potentials, gc_catalog_full.fits and Gaia XP pulls.
  • Several WSDB caches that every stream fit depends on have no builder script.
  • manifest.json and checksums.txt contain stale entries.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
All drawn from the current processed products (bin/plot_data_products.py, ocen plot-data, bin/build_mass_function.py).

The 89 kinematic bins of the baseline fit (colour) and published profiles that are not fitted. Top: HST proper-motion dispersions, radial and tangential (ours, black; oMEGACat VI published, grey) continued outward by our Gaia EDR3 profiles (blue); dashed: the rotation term each fitted profile carries. Bottom left: MUSE line-of-sight dispersion with its rotation term (v_rot/√2). Bottom right: published one-dimensional Gaia proper-motion profiles (Vasiliev & Baumgardt 2021, Baumgardt+2019) against ours; the Vasiliev & Baumgardt profile lies below the HST values inside ~200″. Proper motions in mas/yr (right axis: km/s at 5.43 kpc).

Rotation used in the streaming correction. Left: Vasiliev & Baumgardt 2021 proper-motion rotation curve (median, 16–84% and 2–98%), peaking at 0.25 mas/yr (≈6.4 km/s) near 450″. Right: MUSE line-of-sight rotation amplitude (oMEGACat VI), rising from ~3 to ~7 km/s between 30″ and 300″.

The Poisson star-count products. Left: surface number density, HST F625W < 19 (2–250″, 117,751 stars) and Gaia G < 17 (300–2400″, 18,289 stars including field). Middle: stars per bin. Right: covered fraction of each annulus (≥ 0.995).

The published oMEGACat VI profiles: proper-motion dispersions (combined, radial, tangential), the σ_R/σ_T anisotropy diagnostic (isotropic inside ~100″, radially biased outside), MUSE line-of-sight dispersion and rotation.

Three-dimensional kinematics of the core from the same stars: line-of-sight velocity field with the fitted rotation axis; plane-of-sky versus line-of-sight rotation; the three velocity components; and proper-motion against line-of-sight dispersions, which agree at the adopted distance.

Shape of the light profile: the MGE of the Trager+1995 profile (used as the tracer of the earlier Jeans fits) against star counts from HST oMEGACat, Gaia EDR3 members and Gaia+Pristine members, each anchored where complete. Beyond the Trager data the MGE is an extrapolation.

oMEGACat colour–magnitude diagram, 30–250″, all stars (left) and with both quality flags (right). Dotted: F625W = 18 (turnoff), 19 (count-product limit) and 23 (luminosity-function turnover).

Present-day mass function from the unflagged oMEGACat sample with a MIST 12.5 Gyr isochrone: CMD and ridge line; luminosity functions in five radial zones; mass functions over 0.52–0.78 M☉ with slopes steepening outward (−1.37 to −1.77); the light-following mass per F625W < 19 star for each variant; and the budget in the 60–100″ zone (observed main sequence, extrapolation below 0.52 M☉, evolved stars, white dwarfs).

docs.title: 0. How the baseline DF likelihood consumes its data
docs.text:
• Driver. bin/run_compact_df_recovery.py.
  • prepare-real (lines 229–263) copies proc/kinematics/<count>.json into the run directory and records each sha256 (lines 249–252).
  • It copies the kinematic data_snapshot.json from the --start-from source run.
  • It writes problem.json. The baseline record is photometry: false, counts: [hst, gaia].
  • At run time, lines 63–72 verify the count sha256 and rebuild the DFJointProblem.
  • Frozen inputs. results/df/dftwo_counts_20260923/observed/:
File Size (B) data_snapshot.json 19,656 ocen_counts_gaia_g17.json 3,226 ocen_counts_hst_f625w19.json 5,411 problem.json 717

batch.json records source_commit 36bca6f, gaia_error_floor_masyr 0.0 and distance 5.43 (fixed in the starting config; free between 4.8 and 6.0 in coordinates). - Snapshot chain. The data_snapshot comes from results/df/pilot_no_dm_20260922, whose run.json has data_source = results/fits/rung2_K1_turnover. The sha256 570399f38ab2… is identical in rung1_K1_slice/summary.json and rung2_K1_turnover/summary.json. - Gate output. report.json lists χ² per point by dataset and the count deviance:

Dataset χ²/pt Count deviance / bin hst_pm_radial_ours 2.07 hst_pm_tangential_ours 1.95 muse_los_dispersion 1.31 gaia_edr3_ours_radial 1.55 gaia_edr3_ours_tangential 2.42 ocen_counts_hst_f625w19 4.94 ocen_counts_gaia_g17 2.19

These are start 0. - Default dataset list. src/ocen_dm/cli.py:364 DEFAULT_DATASETS holds the same five kinematic keys. - The note at cli.py:359–363 records why gaia_edr3_pm (published VB21 spline) was replaced on 2026-09-19. - It also records why gaia_dr2_pm was dropped on 2026-09-20. - Duplicate guard. likelihood.py:373 _FORBIDDEN_TOGETHER refuses combinations that share stars, for example published plus "ours" HST, or VB21 plus our Gaia.

docs.title: K1. HST PM dispersion, our measurement (hst_pm_radial_ours, hst_pm_tangential_ours)
docs.text:
• Source. oMEGACat VI (Häberle et al. 2025, ApJ).
  • arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.04903
  • DOI: https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-4357/adbe67
  • Data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14978551
  • Raw file. raw/omegacat_vi_kinematics/catalog_and_selections.fits (260,994,240 B). The published md5 9de5a701… was verified in provenance/manifest.json.
  • Builder. src/ocen_dm/kinematics/hst_profile.py:
  • load_hst_sample (:112)
  • hst_profile (:170)
  • build_hst_profile (:221, writes :243)
  • load_hst_product (:248)
  • Selection.
  • oMEGACat selection_hq_astrometry > 0 (flagged stars only; require_flag=True, correct_unflagged=False).
  • Edges DEFAULT_EDGES = geomspace(2, 250, 21) ∪ [300, 340, 360] arcsec (:101), giving 21 bins (r_median 3.65–341.5″).
  • Each bin is fitted as a cluster 2-D Gaussian plus a field mixture, using the K8 field template in absolute PM.
  • Product. proc/kinematics/ocen_pm_dispersion_hst_ours.ecsv (10,949 B; built 2026-09-20T08:46Z).
  • Columns: r_lower/r_median/r_upper [arcsec], n_stars, n_flagged, f_unflagged, f_field, sigma_pmr(_err), sigma_pmt(_err), sigma_pm(_err) [mas/yr], sigma_raw, sigma_sys, sigma_kms(_err), r_pc, r_node0..7.
  • Metadata: unflagged_bias (1.077, 0.011) is recorded but not applied.
  • Likelihood use. likelihood.py:275 _hst_ours.
  • Errors are symmetric.
  • The tangential component adds ⟨μ_T⟩² from the K5 rotation curve as streaming2. The rotation-curve error is propagated in quadrature (streaming_error_on_sigma, :153).
  • r_nodes gives star-weighted radial averaging.
  • Restrictions.
  • Metadata note: HST PMs are locally corrected, so the dispersion is about a rotation-free mean.
  • Shares stars with K7, so the two cannot be combined (_FORBIDDEN_TOGETHER).
  • Status. a, b (Jeans rung0/1/2). The loader auto-builds the product if it is missing, per the README.

docs.title: K2/K3. MUSE LOS dispersion and LOS rotation
docs.text:
• Source. oMEGACat VI, as for K1.
  • Raw file. raw/omegacat_vi_kinematics/los_profile.fits (17,280 B; md5 verified). The .dat twin (4,237 B) is unused.
  • Builder. src/ocen_dm/data/omegacat.py:257 preprocess (CLI ocen preprocess --dataset omegacat, cli.py:82). The configuration is in configs/data.yaml omegacat_vi.products.
  • Products.
  • proc/kinematics/omegacat_vi_los_dispersion.ecsv (29 rows). r_median 5.66–290.3″ (edges 0–332.3″). Columns sigma_los, sigma_los_err_lo/hi [km/s], plus src_* copies.
  • proc/kinematics/omegacat_vi_los_rotation.ecsv (29 rows). Columns v_rot, v_rot_err_lo/hi [km/s], theta_0 [deg].
  • Likelihood use. likelihood.py:172–203.
  • The two-piece Gaussian handles the asymmetric errors.
  • streaming2 = v_rot²/2 (:182–186), with a check that the bins are identical.
  • No rotation error is propagated for MUSE (module docstring).
  • Metadata rule (ocen_likelihood_rule): "binned profile: compare a model integrated over the same radial bin and tracer selection; bins share stars with other binnings of the same data, so alternative binnings are not independent likelihood factors".
  • Status. a, b.

docs.title: K4. Gaia EDR3 PM dispersion, our measurement (gaia_edr3_ours_radial, gaia_edr3_ours_tangential)
docs.text:
• Source. Vasiliev & Baumgardt (2021), MNRAS 505, 5978.
  • arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.09568
  • DOI: https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stab1475
  • Data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4891252
  • Input. K6 member catalogue.
  • Builder. src/ocen_dm/kinematics/outer_gaia.py:61 build_edr3_profile; load_edr3_profile (:141) auto-builds if missing.
  • Selection.
  • Quality bit 2 (QUALITY_BIT).
  • Mean PM error < 0.4 × the published σ(R). That σ(R) comes from K5 through vb2021_replication.published_profile.
  • Edges [300, 380] ∪ geomspace(460, 2400, 8) arcsec give 9 bins (r_median 357–2149″). Bins with fewer than 25 stars are skipped.
  • Per bin: the K8 field template matched to the bin's error ceiling and G range; exact perspective correction; depth dispersion from the composite tracer L2 (_composite_tracer, :56).
  • Membership probability is not used as a weight.
  • Product. proc/kinematics/ocen_pm_dispersion_edr3_ours.ecsv (7,735 B; built 2026-10-11T07:11Z, with values identical to the 2026-09-23 snapshot).
  • Raw-error columns: sigma_pmr(_err), sigma_pmt(_err).
  • Eta-inflated alternatives: sigma_*_eta(_err).
  • Also mean_pmr, mean_pmt, streaming2, f_field, median_eta, median_g, r_node0..7.
  • Metadata note: sigma_sys (half the raw/eta gap) is not added to the errors.
  • Likelihood use. likelihood.py:308. Defaults: error_model="raw" and rotation="published" (the K5 curve with its percentile error). The variant rotation="ours" uses the fitted mean motion instead.
  • Restrictions. Shares stars with K5, K9 and the combined key gaia_edr3_ours (forbidden together).
  • Status. a, b.

docs.title: K5. Vasiliev & Baumgardt 2021 PM dispersion and rotation profiles
docs.text:
• Raw file. $OCEN_CATALOGUES/vasiliev_baumgardt_2021_clusters.zip (118,940,646 B). This is outside the repo. The published md5 3a07093b… is recorded as verified. The product reads the member profiles/NGC_5139_oCen.txt.

docs.title: C1/C2. Poisson count profiles
docs.text:
• Builder. bin/build_count_profiles.py (hst_counts :71, gaia_counts :112, build :132, main :149). The likelihood is in kinematics/counts.py (CountProfile; schema 1/2 handling in to_dict/from_dict, :174–195).

C1, HST (ocen_counts_hst_f625w19). - Input. raw/omegacat_vi_kinematics/catalog_and_selections.fits. - Selection. All stars with measured F625W < 19 and no quality flag (139,498 stars). - Binning and coverage. Centre pixel (15000, 15000) at 0.04″/px. 20 log bins from 2 to 250″. Coverage from the occupancy of 3″ cells, set to 1 inside 30″. - Field term. fit_field=False. - Rationale (metadata note). The hq flag is 12–15 % radially incomplete; N(<20)/N(<19) = 2.0–2.1 at all radii; the field is below 0.5 % at 250″.

C2, Gaia (ocen_counts_gaia_g17). - Input. K6. - Selection. All stars with G < 17, members plus field (24,695 stars). - Binning. 12 full annuli from 300 to 2400″. - Field term. fit_field=True (a uniform field density is fitted).

Files (both in proc/kinematics/):

File Size (B) Notes ocen_counts_hst_f625w19.ecsv 3,870 schema 2 ocen_counts_hst_f625w19.json 9,132 schema 2, contains node_weights ocen_counts_gaia_g17.ecsv 2,292 schema 2 ocen_counts_gaia_g17.json 5,368 schema 2 ocen_counts_*_schema1_20260923.{ecsv,json} — used by the baseline (sha256 match)
  • ECSV columns. r_lower, r_upper, r_median, n_stars, coverage, area_arcsec2, density_per_arcmin2, poisson_err_per_arcmin2.
  • Consumers. run_compact_df_recovery.py with --counts (baseline; rho20scan_*; mpsscan_*; mocks). Plots: bin/plot_count_profiles.py:38, plot_halo_compensation.py, plot_mass_per_star_profile.py, plot_remnant_halo_degeneracy.py, plot_mock_mass_per_star.py.
  • Likelihood note (counts.py docstring). Schema-1 products are "read for replay only" because their mean is star-weighted, biased high by about 3 % per bin for Σ ∝ R⁻². The baseline and all 2026-09-23 scans used schema 1.
  • Status. a.

docs.title: L1. Trager, King & Djorgovski 1995 surface-brightness profile

docs.title: L2. Composite tracer profile (not a stored product)
docs.text:
• What it is. light_model.composite_profile (:131) / load_tracer_profile("composite") (:165).

docs.title: L3. Baumgardt GC database parameters
docs.text:

docs.title: M1. Present-day mass function and mass per counted star (M/N19)
docs.text:
• Inputs.
  • oMEGACat catalog_and_selections.fits: unflagged stars with F625W and F814W in zones 10–30–60–100–175–250″, with a common fit limit F625W < 21.0.
  • MIST v1.2 bolometric-correction tables, through minimint 0.5.1. HST_ACSWF.txz and HST_WFC3.txz were downloaded from waps.cfa.harvard.edu/MIST/BC_tables/v1/ and prepared into the prefix $OCEN_ISOCHRONES/minimint_hst/. That directory exists (241 MB; 70 filter files plus symlinks to the base grid). See the project journal.
  • Builder. bin/build_mass_function.py:
  • isochrone minimint.Interpolator(["ACS_WFC_F625W", "ACS_WFC_F814W"]) at line 82;
  • 12.5 Gyr, D = 5.43 kpc, E(B−V) = 0.12;
  • [Fe/H] from the ridge-line fit (adopted −1.20) or forced to --feh -1.53.
  • Products.
  • results/mass_function/mass_function_20260923.json (9,262 B).
  • results/mass_function/mass_function_feh153_20260923.json (9,275 B).
  • Keys: age_gyr, feh_adopted, ridge_fits, dm0, a625/a814, m_turnoff, zones and others.
  • Plot: plots/mass_function_*.png.
  • Result (the project journal). M/N19 = 8.4–9.5 M☉ per star in the kinematically dominant zones.
  • Use. An external prior. bin/run_mass_per_star_scan.sh pins the HST count amplitude with --mass-per-star ocen_counts_hst_f625w19=M for M = 7–12, writing results/df/mpsscan_*, mpsmock_* and related plots. It is not part of the baseline.
  • Provenance gap. Not in datasets.yaml. The MIST citation and URL appear only in the project journal.

docs.title: Known gaps and inconsistencies
docs.text:
Found in the 2026-10-13 audit. Each item is open unless marked otherwise.

  1. Baseline counts use the old (schema-1) products. In progress.
  2. dftwo_counts_20260923, rho20scan_* and mpsscan_* used schema-1 counts (star-weighted bin average, biased; see counts.py). Their frozen inputs still replay exactly; the old products are kept as *_schema1_20260923.*.
  3. The canonical ocen_counts_*.json are schema 2 since commit 1af8c33. The base model was refitted with them on 2026-10-13 (results/df/dftwo_counts_area_20261013); the scans have not been rerun.
  4. Docstring and metadata drift.
  5. Fixed 2026-10-13: the bin/build_count_profiles.py docstring described the old quantile nodes.
  6. selection/field_template.py:107 writes "parallax_over_error_max": 5 into the product's cuts metadata, but no parallax cut is applied (parallax_cut: none). The metadata is misleading.
  7. likelihood.py:251 _edr3_ours admits that its note string describes an obsolete construction.
  8. Stale provenance records.
  9. provenance/manifest.json and checksums.txt list vasiliev2021_gc_members/clusters.zip at data/raw/vasiliev2021_gc_members/clusters.zip. That directory is empty, and the copy actually used is the external <code>/apogee_halo_rotation/.../vasiliev_baumgardt_2021_clusters.zip.
  10. The manifest also keeps an obsolete kuzma2026_members.* row with status manual and exists=false, next to the real kuzma2026_members.txt entry.
  11. data/raw/baumgardt_gc_catalogue/ is empty because the file is referenced from CAT, which is intended.
  12. The T3 product's ocen_raw.manifest says unregistered, because it was built before the manifest entry existed.
  13. Registry incomplete.
  14. provenance/datasets.yaml omegacat_vi_kinematics has files: [], although 22 files are downloaded and md5-verified in the manifest.
  15. datasets.yaml omits the following:
    • STREAMFINDER 2021 and 2024, HST LP (all in configs/data.yaml only).
    • Tango Zenodo 4300977, gc_catalog_full.fits, Gaia XP/Andrae pulls.
    • Hunter, Portail, McMillan and MWPotential2014_mod potentials; DB98; GSE contours.
    • MIST/minimint BC tables; the K8 WSDB field template; T2 (covered by product metadata only).
    • Baumgardt+2018 RVs, planned in docs/DATA_GAPS_PLAN.md but never ingested.
  16. Products without builders.
  17. S2 stream5455_gaia_errors.npz, which every stream fit depends on.
  18. S5 XP pulls.
  19. The S1 MRT→FITS conversion, which has no checksum for the FITS.
  20. External path dependencies outside the repository and CAT.
  21. The VB21 zip under <code>/apogee_halo_rotation.
  22. The oCen_bar potentials and GSE contours under OB, reached through two different path conventions.
  23. McMillan17 from the installed AGAMA package, so results depend on the AGAMA version.
  24. Inconsistent systemic values across modules.
  25. μ_sys: cluster.MU_SYS = (−3.257, −6.730); the K8 template frame uses (−3.2514, −6.7444), derived from K6; streams/frames.py uses (−3.2499, −6.7461).
  26. v_los: 232.7 in cluster.py, 232.6 in field_template.py, 232.78 in frames.py and in the Baumgardt registry.
  27. Each choice may be intentional, but none is documented as a single source.
  28. Selection inconsistencies within the light and tracer chain.
  29. L2 (Jeans tracer and K4 depth term) uses oMEGACat selection_hq_f625w star counts inside 25″.
  30. C1 (DF baseline) deliberately avoids that flag as 12–15 % radially incomplete.
  31. K10 hst_quality uses a flag that contains a CMD cut (project journal, 2026-10-08; flagged and not changed).
  32. Unverified references (per datasets.yaml or the project journal):
  33. Trager 1995 ADS link (verified: false).
  34. Baumgardt+2019 DOI (verified: false).
  35. Baumgardt GC database version.
  36. Kuzma+2021 (registered, no data, verified: false).
  37. Hunter+2024 paper.
  38. Origins of the Portail17 and MWPotential2014_mod .ini files.
  39. GSE contours.
  40. Andrae+2023 reference.
  41. The meaning of the VB21 profile undocumented_col12.
  42. Registered or present but unused.
    • The O1 oMEGACat files: alternative binnings, equipartition, .dat twins, notebook.
    • S3 STREAMFINDER 2021.
    • The unused Hunter24 variants, pot_bar_mod, PriceWhelan19/22, MWPotential2014.
    • The large XP catalogues in CAT.
    • datasets.yaml entries with no data: noyola2006_sbp (no NGC 5139 rows), omegacat_ii_astrometry (no files, "not used until validated"), kuzma2021_edr3_tails, youakim2023_debris.
  43. Quarantined stale products.
    • proc/kinematics/_stale_pre_centre_fix/ holds three products built before the 2026-09-19 centre correction: ocen_outer_fit_quality, ocen_pm_dispersion_ours and ocen_pm_dispersion_mixture. Its README says they feed only historical figures.
    • plotting/constraints.py:437 writes a fresh ocen_outer_fit_quality.ecsv to the non-stale path when save=True. None currently exists there.
    • No code reads the other two stale files.
  44. Rebuild date versus snapshot.
    • ocen_pm_dispersion_edr3_ours.ecsv was rebuilt on 2026-10-11, after the baseline. The values were verified identical today, but the loaders auto-build missing products, so a fresh checkout can silently produce data that differ from the frozen snapshots (README:162–165).
    • Run directories freeze their inputs (data_snapshot.json, count JSON with sha256), which protects the recorded runs.
  45. Heavy and uncommitted items.
    • results/streams/m5_gaia_knee.npz (242 MB) is a one-off diagnostic cache.
    • bin/streams/fit_bar_ocen.py has uncommitted edits, and check_stream_coordinate.py (a consumer of S4) is untracked.

docs.title: P1–P7. Potentials and auxiliary model inputs
docs.text:
P1. Hunter+2024 MW potentials. - Location. OB/agama_potentials/MWPotentialHunter24_*.ini, from the oCen_bar clone (github.com/adllmr/oCen_bar per the project journal). - Path conventions. streams/restricted.py:37 HUNTER24_DIR is a relative path; tails/bar_migration.py:25 uses the OCEN_BAR_DIR env variable with default $OCEN_BAR_DIR. - Files used: - axi (73,032 B): restricted.py, lmc.py:63, mw_variants.py:45, bar_migration.py:100 and others. - full (227,828 B): restricted.py:92. - baryon_full and baryon_axi: bar = A × (baryon_full − baryon_axi). - spiral (735,071 B): streams/spiral.py:82. - Unused: nonaxi, rotating, rotspiral, pot_bar_mod, PriceWhelan19/22, MWPotential2014.ini. - Citation. arXiv:2403.18000 (the project journal). the project journal says the paper itself was not retrieved: UNVERIFIED.

P2. Portail17.ini and Portail17_axi.ini (241,764 B and 47,001 B). - Used through opt-in bar_model='portail17' (restricted.py:72,98). - Paper: Portail+2017, arXiv:1608.07954 (project journal). The provenance of the .ini files is UNVERIFIED.

P3. MWPotential2014_mod.ini (469 B). - Used by tails/bar_migration.py:155. Source UNVERIFIED.

P4. McMillan17.ini. - The code uses the AGAMA package copy (site-packages/agama/data/McMillan17.ini, AGAMA 1.0.152) via glob: tails/progenitor_orbits.py:222, restricted.py:114, bin/streams/scope_jacobi.py:39, bin/nbody/run_nbody.py:52. - A second copy exists at OB/agama_potentials/McMillan17.ini (797 B).

P5. DB98_Model1.ini. - File: configs/potentials/DB98_Model1.ini (1,284 B). This is the only file in configs/potentials. - Model: Dehnen & Binney 1998, MNRAS 294, 429, arXiv:astro-ph/9612059, Model 1 (the Ibata+2019 host), built from DB98 Tables 1 and 3. - Checks at the project journal: v_c(R0) = 222.0 km/s; Σ(|z| < 1.1 kpc) = 67.7 M☉ pc⁻². - Consumers: restricted.py, backtrack_fimbulthul.py:34, sgr_*, run_db98_ibata_frame.sh, run_rotation_tests.sh.

P6. Vasiliev, Belokurov & Erkal 2021 "Tango for three" archive. - Location. CAT/vasiliev21_tango_zenodo4300977/. - PROVENANCE.txt records: - MNRAS 501, 2279; arXiv:2009.10726 - https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4300977 (v2; the paper cites v1, 4038141) - md5 151950f0…; downloaded 2026-10-12 - units 232,500 M☉, G = 1, time unit 0.9778 Gyr - Files used: - potentials_{axisym,triax}/trajlmc.txt - accel.txt - potentials_axisym/potential_evolving.ini - mw00.pot - Consumers. bin/streams/lmc_tango_check.py, lmc_vs_tango.py. The LMC parameters in streams/lmc.py follow Tango Section 3.1. - Pitfall (the project journal). AGAMA reorders the components of potential_evolving.ini, so select them by type. - Registration. Not registered anywhere in provenance/ or configs/.

P7. GSE E–Lz contours. - File. OB/artifacts/gaiadr3_gse_elz.fits (17,280 B), labelled "Belokurov+2023" in the project journal with no reference: UNVERIFIED. - Consumer. tails/bar_migration.py:27,157.

Internal tails outputs, not external data. - results/tails/{progenitor_orbits_summary.ecsv, progenitor_orbit_tracks.npz}, from tails/products.py:48. - bar_migration_*, friction_test.ecsv, class2_barred.ecsv, resonances.ecsv, dm_density_grid.ecsv, po_*.ecsv. - The N-body scripts read only results/nbody/<model>/{ics.npz, orbit/snap_today.npz}.

docs.title: Periphery, tails and streams
docs.text: Shorthands are defined on the Data products page.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Every ingested periphery and tail dataset on the sky. Left: the Kuzma & Ishigaki 2025 Gaia+Pristine footprint (5°) and the Fimbulthul candidates of Ibata+2019, 15–27° to the north. Right: the periphery field and members (P > 0.5) with the Kuzma+2026 FLAMES fields (members and non-members).

Kuzma & Ishigaki 2025: proper-motion density of the field and the 2,737 members with P > 0.5.

Kuzma+2026 FLAMES line-of-sight velocities along the tails (signed distance from the centre, trailing negative): 157 members in six fields, with field means against the systemic 232.6 km/s.

Fimbulthul candidates of Ibata+2019 (309 stars): sky positions with proper-motion vectors relative to NGC 5139, and the dereddened CMD.

STREAMFINDER (Ibata+2024) stream 54, the data the stream models are fitted to: 3,724 members on the sky (colour: G); proper motions along the stream in the chord great-circle frame φ1, showing the steepening beyond φ1 ≈ 15° (the "knee"); and the 29 radial velocities.

docs.title: T1/T2. Kuzma & Ishigaki 2025 Pristine periphery and its Gaia covariance
docs.text:
• Source.
  • arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.01135
  • Journal: https://academic.oup.com/mnras/article/537/3/2752/8002861
  • Data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14791430

Free fit goes to \(\rho_{20}=0\) (2026-09-23, old counts) \(\rho_{20}\) profile \(\rho_{20}\) fixed at 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4 M☉ pc⁻³, all else refitted How much DM is allowed at fixed fit quality Δ objective +0.5 … +10.6; a sensitivity curve, not a limit (mocks scatter by ±0.7) Mass-per-star scan HST count amplitude pinned at 8–12 M☉ per F625W < 19 star, free halo How the star/dark split depends on the assumed stellar mass \(\rho_{20}\) ≈ 2–4 at the photometric 8–9, 0 at the dynamical 10.7

Main results, figures and mock tests: DF observed-fit write-up (LaTeX). The halo and scan numbers above use the count products from before the 2026-10-13 fix and have not been rerun.

docs.title: Parameters of each model
docs.text:
The base model has 10 free parameters (7 stellar, 2 remnant, the distance) and 3 profiled count nuisances. The dark-matter variants add a halo; the Jeans model has its own 10 parameters.

Model Parameters beyond the base model Range Fixed Free cored halo \(\rho_{20}\) (DM density at 20 pc), \(r_s\) (scale) 0–10 M☉ pc⁻³; 5–150 pc, log \(\gamma=0\) (core), taper \(r_t=1\) kpc \(\rho_{20}\) profile \(r_s\) 5–150 pc, log \(\rho_{20}\) = 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4 Mass-per-star scan \(\rho_{20}\), \(r_s\) as the free halo HST count amplitude pinned: 8–12 M☉ per counted star

Halo density: \(\rho(r)=\rho_{20}\,(r/20\,{\rm pc})^{-\gamma}\,[(1+r/r_s)/(1+20/r_s)]^{\gamma-3}\,e^{-(r^2-20^2)/r_t^2}\).

What the data constrain. Twelve mocks drawn from the base model recover the total mass to ±3% at 20 pc and ±5% over 2–40 pc, but the recovered \(\rho_{20}\) scatters by 0.5–0.9 M☉ pc⁻³. The leading degeneracy is stellar mass against dark mass (remnants plus halo) through the count amplitude. Pinning the mass per counted star removes it but needs that number to ~3%; the photometric mass function gives 8.3–9.8 M☉ per star against the dynamical 10.7.

Implementation and history.

  • Regularized DF implementation: the DF family, numerics and tests.
  • Anisotropy diagnostics: why the model needs two anisotropy transitions (inner data want radial, outer data tangential anisotropy).
  • Observed-data flexibility: the one-transition DF fails (χ²/N ≈ 4.8).
  • Compact DF proposal (PDF), compact DF recovery, frequency-mapper diagnostic.
  • Earlier mixture DF (superseded): AGAMA DF models, capacity challenge, mass recovery.
  • DF model literature review.
  • Next steps under discussion: Codex review, 2026-10-13 (multi-mass stellar populations, remnant treatment).

docs.title: Base model: two-transition DF, no dark matter
docs.text:
The reference model for the cluster mass distribution. Every dark-matter variant is compared with it.

Status (2026-10-13)

Refitted on 2026-10-13 with the corrected (area-weighted) count likelihood: results/df/dftwo_counts_area_20261013, best job observed_no_halo_start3. The fit is numerically validated but fails its own data-fit gate. It supersedes the 2026-09-23 fit (results/df/dftwo_counts_20260923), whose star-weighted count averages were biased; parameters moved by ≤ 4% and the mass per counted star by −1.8%.

docs.title: All parameters
docs.text:
The fit is a multi-start optimisation (no posterior sampling), so best-fit values are given without uncertainties; mocks drawn from this model recover \(M_\star\) to ±6% and \(M_{\rm rem}\) to ±23% (see below).

Free parameters (10)

docs.title: Stellar DF
docs.text:
The regularized exponential action DF (contour construction of Binney 2026, MNRAS 549, stag854), rebuilt at every iteration and iterated to self-consistency in the total potential (stars + remnants):

\[ f(\mathbf J)=A\,\exp\!\left[-\left(L_c/J_0\right)^{\alpha}\right], \qquad q=J_r+L . \]

The contour label \(L_c\) follows the spherical frequency ratio, biased by the anisotropy function \(b(q)\): \(b>0\) favours radial orbits, \(b<0\) tangential ones. Two transitions:

\[ b(q)=b_{\rm out}\,s(q;J_a)+\left(b_{\rm outer}-b_{\rm out}\right)s(q;J_{\rm outer}), \qquad s(q;J)=\frac{q^2}{q^2+J^2}. \]

The core is isotropic (\(b\to0\) as \(q\to0\)); the model is radially anisotropic at intermediate radii and tangential outside.

Parameter Meaning Range Best fit \(J_0\) envelope scale (pc km/s) 30–800, log 56.0 \(\alpha\) envelope sharpness 0.6–3 0.80 \(b_{\rm out}\) intermediate anisotropy −2 to 2 +0.77 (radial) \(J_a\) first transition (pc km/s) 5–500, log 65.5 \(b_{\rm outer}\) outer anisotropy −4 to 2 −0.33 (tangential) \(J_{\rm outer}\) second transition (pc km/s) 2–100 × \(J_a\) 312

docs.title: How the stellar mass is determined
docs.text:
• Seven stellar parameters: the mass normalisation \(M_\star\) and the six DF parameters (\(J_0\), \(\alpha\), \(b_{\rm out}\), \(J_a\), \(b_{\rm outer}\), \(J_{\rm outer}\)). The stellar density is not an input: it is computed from \(f(\mathbf J)\) in the total potential, so the envelope and the anisotropy parameters together set its shape.
  • The star counts constrain the shape only. Their amplitude (counted stars per unit model surface density) is a nuisance parameter, profiled analytically at every evaluation; the counts say where the stars are, not how much mass they carry.
  • \(M_\star\) is set by the kinematics, jointly with the remnants. It is not taken from photometry. The mass per counted star (10.48 M☉ per F625W < 19 star) is therefore an output of the fit.
  • The only place \(M_\star\) is fixed externally is the mass-per-star scan, where the count amplitude is held at a value from the photometric mass function instead of being profiled.
  • Mass-to-light ratio. With L_V = 1.16×10⁶ L☉ (Harris catalogue V = 3.68 and E(B−V) = 0.12, at the fitted 5.356 kpc), \(M_\star/L_V = 2.6\) and \(M_{\rm tot}/L_V = 2.8\).

docs.title: Remnant component
docs.text:
\[ \rho_{\rm rem}(r)=\frac{3M_{\rm rem}}{4\pi a_{\rm rem}^3} \left(1+\frac{r^2}{a_{\rm rem}^2}\right)^{-5/2} \]

It stands for all mass that does not follow the counted light: neutron stars and stellar-mass black holes, any mass-segregated white dwarfs and heavy stars, and part of the effect of a central black hole. At the best fit it holds 8% of the total mass, has a half-mass radius of \(1.305\,a_{\rm rem}=2.8\) pc, and dominates the mass inside ~1.5 pc (60% inside 1 pc).

docs.title: Distance, geometry, rotation
docs.text:
• Distance free in 4.8–6.0 kpc with a Gaussian prior \(N(5.43, 0.05)\) kpc; best fit 5.356 kpc (1.5σ low).
  • Spherical and non-rotating. The published rotation is removed at the moment level, \(\sigma^2_{\rm pred}=\langle v^2\rangle_{\rm DF}-v^2_{\rm rot}\); a negative result is rejected, never floored.

The count amplitude converts to a mass per counted star: the best fit has 10.48 M☉ of light-following mass per F625W < 19 star (10.67 in the 2026-09-23 fit). Details of every product: Data products.

The HST count residuals remain structured: the data lie below the model near 1 pc and in the outermost HST bin (~6 pc), with deviance residuals of about −4, and above it at 3–4 pc (+4.6).

Counts (HST and Gaia), MUSE line-of-sight and HST/Gaia proper-motion dispersions against the 2026-10-13 (blue) and 2026-09-23 (orange) fits, with the earlier Jeans model (dashed). Bottom row: residuals; the count panel shows signed Poisson deviance residuals. Both fits are evaluated with the corrected count likelihood.

docs.title: Comparison with the Jeans model (dashed curves)
docs.text:
Full description, figures and posterior: Jeans comparison model.

The dashed curves are the best rung-2 spherical Jeans fit without dark matter (results/fits/rung2_K1_turnover), the best model of the earlier Jeans ladder. Both models are fitted to the same 89-bin kinematic snapshot, so their kinematic χ² compare directly; the Jeans fit uses a fixed light profile (an MGE of the Trager+1995 profile joined to HST star counts) instead of the Poisson star counts.

Jeans (rung 2, no DM) DF base model Stellar tracer and mass MGE light profile, mass-to-light free self-consistent action DF Free stellar parameters \(M_\star\) only (density shape fixed by the light) \(M_\star\) and six DF parameters (shape fitted to the counts) Anisotropy turnover β(r): β₀ = −0.50 (centre) → +0.20 → −0.98 (outside) isotropic core → +0.15 near 8 pc → −0.53 at 100 pc Central black hole 4.4×10⁴ M☉ (16–84%: 3.9–4.6×10⁴) none \(M_\star\) 2.37×10⁶ M☉ 3.00×10⁶ M☉ Remnants (Plummer) 7.7×10⁵ M☉, a = 5.7 pc 2.7×10⁵ M☉, a = 2.2 pc Total mass 3.18×10⁶ M☉ 3.26×10⁶ M☉ \(M_\star/L_V\), \(M_{\rm tot}/L_V\) 2.0, 2.7 (ML); 2.3, 2.8 (median) 2.6, 2.8 Distance 5.34 kpc 5.36 kpc χ² (per bin) Jeans DF HST PM radial (21) 61.8 (2.94) 42.6 (2.03) HST PM tangential (21) 36.6 (1.74) 39.8 (1.89) MUSE LOS (29) 51.7 (1.78) 38.1 (1.31) Gaia PM radial (9) 16.9 (1.88) 14.4 (1.60) Gaia PM tangential (9) 23.0 (2.56) 21.5 (2.39) Total (89) 190.0 156.4
  • The DF fits better overall (Δχ² = 34) and in every dataset except the HST tangential proper motions.
  • The Jeans model follows the central rise of the HST proper-motion dispersions inside 0.3 pc (~11″), which the DF, with an isotropic core and no black hole, stays below by 1.5–2.4σ in several bins: χ² = 7.3 (Jeans) against 21.5 (DF) for those 10 bins. This is where the black hole matters.
  • It pays for this at intermediate radii: at 2–20 pc (36 bins of HST, MUSE and Gaia) χ² = 122.2 (Jeans) against 77.8 (DF), mostly in the HST radial proper motions (40.2 against 20.2) and the MUSE line-of-sight dispersions (30.9 against 18.7).
  • The black hole is tied to an imposed anisotropy. A cored stellar density around a point mass needs β₀ ≤ −½ for any non-negative DF; the prior enforces it and the fit sits at the bound (β₀ = −0.503). Even so, under the standard separable construction a non-negative DF fails to exist at 0.02–0.18 pc, where the black hole dominates (89.7% of posterior draws fail; no failure outside ~0.2 pc; a non-separable DF is not excluded; DF consistency audit). The DF base model is non-negative by construction.
  • Both put about the same total mass in the cluster (3.2–3.3×10⁶ M☉) but divide it differently: the Jeans fit has 20% less stellar mass and nearly three times more remnant mass, spread over a 2.5× larger scale. This is the same stars-versus-dark-mass degeneracy seen within the DF fits.
  • Why \(M_\star\) differs by 11% at the same total mass. In neither model is the stellar mass fixed by the light or the counts; it is the normalisation the kinematics leave after the remnants (and, for Jeans, the black hole and the imposed central anisotropy) take their share. The remnant mass is close to the total minus \(M_\star\), so with remnants at 8–17% of the total, a 1% change in \(M_\star\) moves \(M_{\rm rem}\) by ~10%.
  • A central black hole was not supported by the DF fits on binned data (September step 3); whether the inner rise needs one, or radially biased central orbits, or mass segregation, is not settled.

docs.title: Properties of the fitted model
docs.text:
By component: (a) density; (b) enclosed mass with half-mass radii dotted; (c) circular velocity; (d) remnant share, local and cumulative; (e) dynamical-to-stellar mass ratio. Grey: outside the radial range of the kinematic data (0.1–63 pc).

(a) Intrinsic radial and tangential dispersions; (b) anisotropy β(r); (c) stellar surface density with half-mass radii; (d) projected line-of-sight and proper-motion dispersions from the DF (before the published rotation is subtracted).

(a) Intrinsic moments; (b) anisotropy bias b(q) over the action distributions of the HST/MUSE and Gaia stars; (c) f(J_r, L).

Key numbers (current fit): stellar half-mass radius 10.4 pc (projected 7.7 pc), remnant half-mass radius 2.8 pc; remnants 66% of the central density; \(M_{\rm tot}/M_\star\) from 2.9 in the centre to 1.09 overall; peak circular velocity 27.0 km/s at 9 pc; central dispersion 21.4 km/s; β peaks at +0.15 near 8 pc and reaches −0.53 at 100 pc. Interpretation: Results.

docs.title: What has been tested
docs.text:
• Convergence: 4 of 6 starts valid (2 Latin starts infeasible), all four reach the same minimum (objectives within 0.01); no parameter at a bound.
  • Numerics: grid refinement shifts predictions by 0.0005σ; direct projection checks agree to ≤ 5×10⁻⁴ in Σ, LOS, PM_R and PM_T.
  • Estimator recovery (2026-09-23 fit, old count likelihood): 12 mocks drawn from this model with published kinematic noise and Poisson counts recover the total mass to ±3% at 20 pc and ±5% over 2–40 pc, \(M_\star\) to ±6%, \(M_{\rm rem}\) to ±23%.

Not yet tested: mocks whose truth breaks the model's own assumptions (mass segregation, rotation, another remnant shape); calibration of the error bars.

docs.title: Built-in assumptions
docs.text:
1. Mass follows light: one stellar DF is both tracer and mass.
  2. Isotropic core.
  3. One remnant component with a fixed Plummer shape.
  4. No central black hole.
  5. Spherical; rotation subtracted from published curves.
  6. Published error bars taken as they are.

docs.title: Jeans comparison model: no dark matter, free black hole
docs.text:
The best model of the earlier Jeans ladder (rung 2, results/fits/rung2_K1_turnover). It is shown as the dashed curve in the base-model figures and is the reference for the question of a central black hole. It is fitted to the same 89-bin kinematic snapshot as the DF base model, so the kinematic χ² of the two compare directly.

Status

Completed 2026-09-21 (nested sampling, 15,972 posterior samples). Current: it uses the same 89-bin kinematic snapshot as the DF base model and its likelihood replays exactly; the 2026-10-13 count-likelihood fix does not apply to it, because it uses a fixed light profile as its tracer, not the star counts. Physically consistent outside the central ~0.2 pc; inside, the standard separable DF construction fails (below).

docs.title: Model definition
docs.text:
Jeans equation. For a spherical tracer of density \( u(r)\) in a mass profile \(M(<r)\) with anisotropy \( eta(r)\),

\[ rac{d( u\sigma_r^2)}{dr}+ rac{2 eta}{r} u\sigma_r^2=- u rac{GM(<r)}{r^2}, \qquad u\sigma_r^2(r)= rac{1}{g(r)}\int_r^\infty g(s)\, u(s) rac{GM(<s)}{s^2}\,ds, \]

with \(g(r)=\exp\left(2\int^r eta/t\,dt ight)\). The line-of-sight and radial and tangential proper-motion dispersions follow from the standard projection integrals (Binney & Mamon 1982; van der Marel 1994) and are averaged over each bin as for the DF. The published rotation is subtracted from the model's second moments exactly as in the DF fit. Solver: src/ocen_dm/kinematics/jeans.py.

Tracer. Fixed, not fitted: an 11-component multi-Gaussian expansion of the composite light profile (oMEGACat star counts inside 25″, Trager+1995 outside; fit residual 0.18 mag rms), deprojected spherically.

Mass components.

Component Form Parameters Stars mass follows the MGE light \(M_\star\) Remnants Plummer sphere \(M_{ m rem}\), \(a_{ m rem}\) Black hole point mass at the centre \(M_{ m BH}\) Dark matter none —

docs.title: How the stellar mass is determined
docs.text:
• One stellar parameter, \(M_\star\): the mass normalisation of the fixed light profile, i.e. the stellar mass-to-light ratio. The stellar density shape is the MGE and is not fitted.
  • The anisotropy parameters do not change the density. They describe the stars' velocities only (unlike in the DF, where they also shape the density).
  • \(M_\star\) is set by the kinematics, jointly with the remnants, the black hole and the anisotropy; it is not taken from photometry.
  • Mass-to-light ratio. With L_V = 1.16×10⁶ L☉ (Harris V = 3.68, E(B−V) = 0.12, at the fitted distance), \(M_\star/L_V\) = 2.0 at maximum likelihood and 2.3 at the posterior median; \(M_{\rm tot}/L_V\) = 2.7–2.8, the same as the DF base model (2.8).

Anisotropy ("turnover"). Three levels joined by two smooth transitions (src/ocen_dm/kinematics/anisotropy.py):

\[ \beta(r)=\beta_0(1-f_1)+\beta_{\rm mid}(f_1-f_2)+\beta_\infty f_2, \qquad f_i=\frac{r^2}{r^2+r_i^2},\quad r_2=r_1+\Delta r . \]

The weights are non-negative and sum to one, so β never leaves the range of its three levels.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
# Parameter Meaning Prior Posterior median (16–84%) Maximum likelihood 1 \(M_{\rm BH}\) [M☉] central black hole (point mass) log-uniform 10²–3×10⁵ 4.25 (3.92–4.58) ×10⁴ 4.41×10⁴ 2 \(M_\star\) [M☉] stellar mass (normalisation of the light profile, i.e. M/L) log-uniform 10⁶–10⁷ 2.66 (2.49–2.85) ×10⁶ 2.37×10⁶ 3 \(M_{\rm rem}\) [M☉] remnant (Plummer) mass log-uniform 10⁴–3×10⁶ 5.4 (3.8–7.0) ×10⁵ 7.7×10⁵ 4 \(a_{\rm rem}\) [pc] remnant Plummer scale log-uniform 0.3–20 5.3 (4.8–5.6) 5.7 5 \(\beta_0\) central anisotropy (<0 tangential; ≤ −½ required with a black hole) uniform −1 to −0.5 −0.53 (−0.57 to −0.51) −0.50 6 \(\beta_{\rm mid}\) intermediate anisotropy level (>0 radial) uniform −1 to 1 0.19 (0.18–0.21) 0.20 7 \(\beta_\infty\) outer anisotropy level uniform −1 to 1 −0.81 (−0.94 to −0.63) −0.98 8 \(r_1\) [pc] first anisotropy transition radius log-uniform 0.05–30 1.09 (0.98–1.20) 1.16 9 \(\Delta r=r_2-r_1\) [pc] gap to the second transition radius log-uniform 0.5–150 38 (33–43) 44 10 D [kpc] distance normal 5.43 ± 0.05 5.36 (5.34–5.38) 5.34

Fit: χ²_kin = 190.0 for 89 bins at maximum likelihood (DF base model: 156.4); ln Z = 85.96. Sampler: UltraNest, 400 live points, Δln Z = 0.5, slice steps 2 × ndim, seed 42.

The upper bound of the β₀ prior is physical, not empirical: a cored tracer around a point mass has a non-negative distribution function only if β₀ ≤ −½ (An & Evans 2006). The posterior piles up against that bound.

docs.title: Mass components
docs.text:
(a) Enclosed mass by component (Jeans: posterior median and 16–84% from 300 saved draws; DF base model dashed). (b) Circular velocity. (c) Non-stellar share of the enclosed mass. Grey: outside the radial range of the data.

  • The black hole dominates the centre. It holds more than half of the enclosed mass out to 1.3 pc; the stars and remnants inside 0.3 pc add only ~560 M☉. The circular velocity therefore rises towards the centre (Keplerian, 43 km/s at 0.1 pc), whereas in the DF model it falls to zero.
  • Beyond ~3 pc the two models agree on the total mass to within a few per cent (Jeans 3.24×10⁶ M☉ in total, DF 3.26×10⁶) and on the circular-velocity peak (~27–28 km/s near 9 pc).
  • They split the non-stellar mass differently. The Jeans model puts 5×10⁵ M☉ in a Plummer of 5.3 pc plus the 4×10⁴ M☉ black hole; the DF puts 2.7×10⁵ M☉ in a Plummer of 2.2 pc. At 10 pc the non-stellar share is ~23% (Jeans) against 15% (DF).

docs.title: Anisotropy
docs.text:
β(r) of the Jeans model (posterior median, 16–84% and 2–98% from 3,000 draws; transition radii r₁ and r₂ dotted) against the DF base model (dashed). Shaded: radial ranges of the HST/MUSE and Gaia data.

  • Inside ~1 pc the models differ in sign. The Jeans model is tangential (β ≈ −0.52 at the centre, −0.48 at 0.3 pc, −0.20 at 1 pc), as the black hole requires; the DF core is isotropic.
  • Between 3 and 15 pc they agree: mildly radial, peaking at β ≈ +0.15.
  • Outside ~20 pc both turn tangential; the Jeans model more strongly (−0.67 at 100 pc against −0.53), where only the Gaia data constrain it.

docs.title: Posterior and degeneracies
docs.text:
Posterior of the black-hole mass and the parameters it trades against (15,972 samples; dashed lines: 16, 50 and 84%).

  • M_BH is well bounded within this model: 4.25×10⁴ M☉, 95% interval 3.6–4.9×10⁴; no posterior sample is below 10⁴ M☉.
  • β₀ is pinned at its bound (−0.525, +0.019/−0.042), so the black-hole mass is measured conditional on the most radial central anisotropy the model allows.
  • M_BH correlates with the remnant scale and r₁ (correlation +0.53 and +0.51): a more extended remnant component or a larger tangential core needs a heavier black hole.
  • The leading degeneracy is stars against remnants (M_rem–M★ −0.95, M_rem–a_rem +0.94), the same stars-versus-dark-mass trade seen in the DF fits.

docs.title: Central bins
docs.text:
Bins inside 2 pc: HST radial and tangential proper-motion dispersions and MUSE line-of-sight dispersions, with the Jeans (solid) and DF (dashed) predictions and residuals.

Data inside 2 pc Bins χ² Jeans χ² DF HST PM radial 13 21.5 22.3 HST PM tangential 13 16.7 23.1 MUSE line of sight 17 20.8 19.4 Total 43 59.0 64.8
  • The black hole gains Δχ² ≈ 6 in the central 43 bins, almost entirely from the tangential proper motions inside 0.3 pc, where the data rise to 0.81–0.86 mas/yr and the DF stays at 0.76.
  • It overshoots the tangential dispersions at 0.4–1.4 pc (residuals −1 to −2.5σ), and the MUSE dispersions do not discriminate.
  • Over all 89 bins the DF fits better by Δχ² = 34, mostly at 2–20 pc; see Comparison with the Jeans model.

docs.title: Physical consistency
docs.text:
Checks from the DF consistency audit, which tests necessary conditions for a non-negative stellar distribution function (passing them is not a proof that one exists):

Check Result Spatial density of every component non-negative everywhere Central condition with a black hole and a cored tracer, β₀ ≤ −½ met (enforced by the prior; β₀ = −0.503) Separable DF, first derivative (B₁) passes everywhere Separable DF, radial condition (R₂) passes everywhere Separable DF, second derivative (B₂) fails at 0.02–0.18 pc (minimum −0.11 at 0.12 pc); 89.7% of posterior draws fail in the same region
  • Outside the central ~0.2 pc no failure is found.
  • Inside it, the standard separable construction gives no non-negative DF. A non-separable DF with the same density and dispersions is not excluded, so the model is not shown to be unphysical there, only not shown to be physical.
  • That region is where the black hole dominates the mass and where its evidence comes from (the central bins above), which is why the result matters for the black-hole question.
  • The DF base model is non-negative by construction.

docs.title: What this model says about a black hole
docs.text: Within the Jeans framework the central rise of the HST proper-motion dispersions is fitted by a 4×10⁴ M☉ point mass with tangential central orbits. The evidence is local (Δχ² ≈ 6 from a few bins inside 0.3 pc), it depends on an anisotropy forced to its physical limit, and in the central ~0.2 pc, where the black hole acts, the standard separable construction of a non-negative distribution function fails. Alternatives that are not yet tested in the DF framework are a point mass with a self-consistent DF, radially biased orbits in the core, and mass segregation of the remnants.

docs.title: Distances to omega Cen stream (Fimbulthul) stars: literature (2026-10-10)
docs.text:
Research agent read full texts (arXiv PDFs); key quotes spot-checked by me in the extracted texts (Ibata+2019 Fig. 3a caption "offset by 0.7 magnitudes ... ~1.5 kpc closer than omega Cen"; Methods "mean distance to these stars of 4.1 kpc, as predicted by the STREAMFINDER algorithm"; Fig. 1 = 0.265 +- 0.008 mas; Ibata+2021 table note "column 9 provides the distance to the star dSF estimated by the algorithm").

  • No standard-candle or spectroscopic distance gradient exists along Fimbulthul. All along-stream distances come from STREAMFINDER: PARSEC SSP template (12.5 Gyr, fixed [Fe/H] per run) fitted to Gaia photometry; weak parallax term from Ibata+2021 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.05245, Eq. 2). Authors note a distance-metallicity degeneracy and multiple distance solutions.
  • Ibata+2019 Nature Astronomy (https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.09544): stream ~0.7 mag brighter than omega Cen in the CMD (Fig. 3a), ~4.1 kpc (STREAMFINDER mean); = 0.265 +- 0.008 mas (DR2, no contamination correction); omega Cen 5630 +- 100 pc (Braga+2018).
  • Ibata, Malhan & Martin 2019 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.07566): Fimbulthul anchor-point distance 4.22 +- 0.01 kpc (orbit fit). Extinction SFD98 + Schlafly & Finkbeiner 2011.
  • Ibata+2021: per-star dSF (DR2 run; local streamfinder_ibata2021_edr3.fits, Fimbulthul = Stream 16). Agent's reduction: dSF falls from ~5.5 kpc (l ~ -57) to ~3.0 kpc (l ~ -29); knee box (b 30-42, l -55..-40) median 4.1 kpc (16-84%: 3.6-4.7), median EDR3 plx 0.248 mas.
  • Ibata+2024 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.17202; our catalogue): no distance column (G0, (BP-RP)0 dereddened); distances only as the Fig. 3 map; stream 55 "~3 kpc".
  • Simpson+2020 GALAH (https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.01548): assumed (m-M)0 = 12.9 (3.8 kpc) for the Ibata sample vs 13.7 for omega Cen.
  • Kuzma+2021 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.02531): 3 RR Lyrae within 5 deg: 5.2 +- 0.6 kpc. Kuzma+2026 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23474): omega Cen dynamical 5.29 +- 0.2 kpc; no tail distances.
  • Malhan+2022 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.07660): weighted-mean parallax (Lindegren zero-point), no gradient.
  • Youakim+2023 quotes "Fimbulthul spans 2.4-7.2 kpc (Malhan+2022)": UNVERIFIED (not found in Malhan+2022). Full per-paper notes: the agent report (session); PDFs/text in the session scratchpad.

    • Implication for this project: the literature puts the knee at ~0.70-0.75 of omega Cen's distance; our CMD-shift track (stream54_cmd_distance.py, relative to members at b 15-20) gives 0.88-0.92 and is the outlier.

docs.title: codex T1T2 next steps 2026 10 10
docs.text: The premise needs one correction: the frame swap changes \(z_\odot\) as well as \(V_{\odot,y}\) and \(R_0\): 0 to 17 pc, 252.24 to 232.24 km/s, and 8.178 to 8.122 kpc (frames.py:16–18). The T1 script supplies distance explicitly, so the frame’s default cluster distance is overridden (sun_dist_bar_grids.py:18–20, grid4_common.py:40–49).

docs.title: Direct answers
docs.text:
(a) T1 is not a projection-only test. make_spray uses one frame both to convert the cluster’s observed state into the model-frame initial condition and to convert the resulting debris back to observables (grid4_common.py:40–50). Thus the swap changes the inferred Galactocentric orbit and the projection. The host setup is unchanged for these runs, but the cluster’s initial state in that host is not (grid4_common.py:46–49; restricted.py:68–84).

For a fixed Galactocentric trajectory at 4 kpc, a 20 km/s transverse observer-velocity shift corresponds to about 1.05 mas/yr, so projection alone is large enough in scale to matter. But T1 does not hold that trajectory fixed: its frame change also alters the initial condition. The packet reports that at \(d=5.6\) kpc the W–R16 gap changes from −782 to −93 in the two frames, with W’s gain concentrated in the outer segment and losses near the cluster; those figures are reported results, not independently recomputed here (packet:2025–2034). They do not isolate reflex from orbit changes.

(b) The proposed decomposition is the right idea, but implement it as two independent frame choices. Cross initial-condition frame with projection frame: Baumgardt IC/Baumgardt projection, Baumgardt IC/Ibata projection, Ibata IC/Baumgardt projection, Ibata IC/Ibata projection. Run at a fixed distance first; then repeat at the alternative distance if needed. The current API cannot express this: make_spray has only one frame argument (grid4_common.py:40–50). Save the model-frame particle states and reproject those same trajectories under both projection frames; this avoids duplicate integrations for the projection-only comparison.

A host \(v_c(R_0)\) sweep is a separate experiment, not a prerequisite for this decomposition. The packet reports the host at 228.8 km/s, while the Ibata frame’s stated solar velocity is constructed using 220 km/s plus 12.24 km/s peculiar motion (packet:2020–2025, frames.py:7–8, 16–18). That mismatch matters when interpreting a physically self-consistent solar-motion model. Test it separately by varying host normalization and solar motion together under a stated relation, while keeping the observed heliocentric cluster data fixed.

(c) Cost-aware order:

  1. Run the IC × projection factorial at one distance, preferably 5.6 kpc, then at 5.43 kpc if the result depends on IC frame. Decision rule: if the score gain follows projection frame with either IC, reflex/projection dominates; if it follows IC with either projection, orbit changes dominate; if there is a large interaction, the effects are coupled.
